1.name: Spellcasting
1.notes:
You learn to channel the magic of nature to cast Ranger spells.

Spell Slots. The Ranger Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast level 1+ spells. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a Long Rest.

Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare a list of Ranger spells of level 1+ that you can cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 spells (Cure Wounds and Ensnaring Strike are recommended). Your number of prepared spells increases as you gain Ranger levels, as shown in the class table. Prepared spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.
If another Ranger feature grants you spells that are always prepared, they don’t count against your number of prepared spells.

Changing Prepared Spells. When you finish a Long Rest, you may replace one prepared spell with another Ranger spell you can cast.

Spellcasting Ability. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability.

Spellcasting Focus. You can use a Druidic Focus as a Spellcasting Focus for your Ranger spells.

1.name: Favored Enemy
1.notes:
You always have the Hunter’s Mark spell prepared. You can cast it twice without expending a spell slot, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
You gain additional free uses of Hunter’s Mark at higher levels, as shown in the class table.

1.name: Weapon Mastery
1.notes:
You can use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency.
Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you may change the weapon types whose mastery properties you can use (for example, switching from Longbows and Shortswords to Scimitars and Longswords).

2.name: Deft Explorer
2.notes:
Your journeys have strengthened your survival skills.

Expertise. Choose one of your skill proficiencies with which you lack Expertise; you gain Expertise in that skill.

Languages. You learn two additional languages of your choice from the standard language lists.

2.name: Fighting Style
2.notes:
You gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice.

Alternatively, you may choose Druidic Warrior: you learn two Druid cantrips (Guidance and Starry Wisp are recommended). These cantrips count as Ranger spells for you, and Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for them. Whenever you gain a Ranger level, you may replace one of these cantrips with another Druid cantrip.

3.name: Subclass Feature
3.notes:
You choose a Ranger subclass and gain its level 3 feature. You gain additional subclass features at higher Ranger levels.

4.name: Ability Score Improvement
4.notes: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Ranger levels 8, 12, and 16.

5.name: Extra Attack
5.notes: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

6.name: Roving
6.notes: Your Speed increases by 10 feet while you aren’t wearing Heavy armor. You also gain a Climb Speed and a Swim Speed equal to your walking Speed.

7.name: Subclass Feature
7.notes:
You gain a level 7 feature from your Ranger subclass.

No Subclass Selected
Select a subclass to view its feature(s) here.

8.name: Ability Score Improvement
8.notes: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

9.name: Expertise
9.notes: Choose two skill proficiencies with which you lack Expertise. You gain Expertise in both skills.

10.name: Tireless
10.notes:
Primal energies bolster you during long journeys.

Temporary Hit Points. As a Magic action, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to 1d8 + your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1). You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once). You regain all uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Decrease Exhaustion. Whenever you finish a Short Rest, your Exhaustion level (if any) is reduced by 1.

11.name: Subclass Feature
11.notes:
You gain a level 11 feature from your Ranger subclass.

No Subclass Selected
Select a subclass to view its feature(s) here.

12.name: Ability Score Improvement
12.notes: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

13.name: Relentless Hunter
13.notes: Taking damage does not break your Concentration on Hunter’s Mark.

14.name: Nature's Veil
14.notes:
As a Bonus Action, you can give yourself the Invisible condition until the end of your next turn.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

15.name: Subclass Feature
15.notes:
You gain a level 15 feature from your Ranger subclass.

No Subclass Selected

16.name: Ability Score Improvement
16.notes: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

17.name: Precise Hunter
17.notes: You have Advantage on attack rolls against the creature currently affected by your Hunter’s Mark.

18.name: Feral Senses
18.notes: You gain Blindsight with a range of 30 feet.

19.name: Epic Boon
19.notes: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Dimensional Travel is recommended.

20.name: Foe Slayer
20.notes: The damage die of your Hunter’s Mark increases to a d10 instead of a d6.
